newsitem.title: USA: Rebels seen taking Kinshasa in one to two days.
newsitem.headline: Rebels seen taking Kinshasa in one to two days.

text.p: U.S. officials said Monday that it may only be one or two days before rebels led by Laurent Kabila take over the Zairean capital, Kinshasa.

Rebel forces are reported to be 60-100 km (38-62 miles) from Kinshasa -- only "a day or two" if Kabila decided to invade the city, one official said. "He'll be coming. There's no doubt about it," the official told Reuters.
Kabila met ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko on a South African navy ship Sunday. They disagreed on arrangements for Mobutu to step down but agreed to meet again within eight to 10 days.
Mobutu wants to hand over power to a transitional body while Kabila wants to take over full control immediately.

The U.S. officials told Reuters that as one condition for his departure, Mobutu said in a letter to President Bill Clinton that if he left power, he wanted assurances "some of his financial resources would remain intact."
"We can't deliver that for him," one official said.
